paragraphs.title: Around Mount Seir and Turning North

easy.question: In which direction did the Israelites travel after turning from the route?
answers: By way of the Red Sea
By way of Egypt
By way of Babylon
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says that they traveled through the wilderness by way of the Red Sea.

easy.question: In which direction did the Lord command them to turn?
answers: South
North
West
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “Turn you northward.”

easy.question: Who lived in the land of Seir?
answers: The descendants of Lot
The Israelites
The descendants of Esau
easy.explanation: The passage says that the descendants of Esau lived in Seir.

medium.question: Why were the Israelites commanded not to meddle with the descendants of Esau?
answers: Because the land of Seir had been given to Esau as a possession
Because the descendants of Esau had left the land
Because the Israelites were not in the wilderness
medium.explanation: The Lord said He would not give Israel any of Esau’s land because He had given Mount Seir to Esau as a possession.

medium.question: What does “Meddle not with them” mean in this passage?
answers: Trade with them
Do not provoke or fight them
Follow them
medium.explanation: The command appears with the prohibition against taking their land, so it means not to provoke them or make war against them.

medium.question: What was the order of events described in these verses?
answers: They bought food, received the command, and then traveled in the wilderness
They turned north, and then received the command to pass through Esau’s border
They traveled around Mount Seir, were told to turn north, and then received instructions about passing through Esau’s territory
medium.explanation: First they traveled around Mount Seir, then the Lord told them to turn north, and finally He gave instructions about passing through the land of Esau.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “they shall be afraid of you” together with “Meddle not with them”?
answers: Israel was to be cautious but not take advantage of their fear to fight them
Israel had to avoid all the descendants of Esau and could not pass through their land
Israel had to conquer the land before Esau attacked
challenge.explanation: The verses say that Esau’s descendants would fear Israel, but Israel was still commanded to be careful and not begin a war.

challenge.question: What is the meaning of “thou hast lacked nothing” after forty years in the wilderness?
answers: The Israelites did not need food or water
The Lord cared for them, and they lacked nothing essential
The Israelites did not move from place to place
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes that the Lord was with Israel in the wilderness and provided for them throughout the forty years.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the command to buy food and water from the descendants of Esau?
answers: The Israelites received Seir without payment
The descendants of Esau had to provide Israel with food for free
Israel had to respect their ownership and pay for what they needed
challenge.explanation: Buying food and water shows that Israel was not to take Esau’s property but was to pay fairly for what it needed.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “they shall be afraid of you” together with “Meddle not with them”?
answers: Israel was to be cautious but not take advantage of their fear to fight them
Israel had to avoid all the descendants of Esau and could not pass through their land
Israel had to conquer the land before Esau attacked
questions.explanation: The verses say that Esau’s descendants would fear Israel, but Israel was still commanded to be careful and not begin a war.

questions.question: What is the meaning of “thou hast lacked nothing” after forty years in the wilderness?
answers: The Israelites did not need food or water
The Lord cared for them, and they lacked nothing essential
The Israelites did not move from place to place
questions.explanation: The verse emphasizes that the Lord was with Israel in the wilderness and provided for them throughout the forty years.

questions.question: What can be understood from the command to buy food and water from the descendants of Esau?
answers: The Israelites received Seir without payment
The descendants of Esau had to provide Israel with food for free
Israel had to respect their ownership and pay for what they needed
questions.explanation: Buying food and water shows that Israel was not to take Esau’s property but was to pay fairly for what it needed.

paragraphs.title: Passing Through Esau’s Territory and Remembering Earlier Peoples

easy.question: Who lived in Seir?
answers: The descendants of Esau
The descendants of Lot
The Horims
easy.explanation: Verse 8 says that the descendants of Esau lived in Seir.

easy.question: What did the Lord command Israel concerning Moab?
answers: Conquer their land
Do not fight them
Demand tribute from them
easy.explanation: The Lord said, “Distress not the Moabites, neither contend with them in battle.”

easy.question: Where did Israel turn after passing by the descendants of Esau?
answers: To the land of Seir
To the land of Edom
By way of the wilderness of Moab
easy.explanation: Verse 8 says, “we turned and passed by the way of the wilderness of Moab.”

medium.question: Why did the Lord not give Israel the land of Moab?
answers: Because He had given it to the descendants of Lot
Because it was too small
Because the Moabites had asked for it
medium.explanation: The Lord said that Ar was an inheritance He had given to the descendants of Lot.

medium.question: Who lived in the land of Moab before the Moabites?
answers: The Horims
The Emims
The descendants of Esau
medium.explanation: The Emims had lived there formerly, before the Moabites.

medium.question: What does “Distress not the Moabites” mean in this passage?
answers: Do not bless Moab
Do not leave Moab
Do not harm or attack Moab
medium.explanation: It appears together with “neither contend with them in battle,” so it means not to harm or attack them.

challenge.question: What similarity between the descendants of Esau and Israel is highlighted in verse 12?
answers: Both inherited a land after earlier peoples had lived there
Both fought against the Moabites
Both were descendants of the Horims
challenge.explanation: The descendants of Esau inherited Seir from the Horims, and the verse compares this with Israel’s inheritance of its land.

challenge.question: What general idea can be inferred from the descriptions of Moab and Seir?
answers: All peoples always remained in their original lands
Different peoples inherited lands after earlier peoples had lived there
Israel conquered all the surrounding lands
challenge.explanation: The verses describe the Emims and Horims as earlier inhabitants and Moab and Esau’s descendants as their successors.

challenge.question: What relationship is described among the Rephaim, the giants, and the Emims?
answers: The Rephaim were descendants of Esau
The Emims conquered the Rephaim
The Rephaim were considered like the giants, and the Moabites called them Emims
challenge.explanation: The passage says that the Rephaim were considered like the Anakims and that the Moabites called them Emims.

questions.question: What similarity between the descendants of Esau and Israel is highlighted in verse 12?
answers: Both inherited a land after earlier peoples had lived there
Both fought against the Moabites
Both were descendants of the Horims
questions.explanation: The descendants of Esau inherited Seir from the Horims, and the verse compares this with Israel’s inheritance of its land.

questions.question: What general idea can be inferred from the descriptions of Moab and Seir?
answers: All peoples always remained in their original lands
Different peoples inherited lands after earlier peoples had lived there
Israel conquered all the surrounding lands
questions.explanation: The verses describe the Emims and Horims as earlier inhabitants and Moab and Esau’s descendants as their successors.

questions.question: What relationship is described among the Rephaim, the giants, and the Emims?
answers: The Rephaim were descendants of Esau
The Emims conquered the Rephaim
The Rephaim were considered like the giants, and the Moabites called them Emims
questions.explanation: The passage says that the Rephaim were considered like the Anakims and that the Moabites called them Emims.

paragraphs.title: Crossing the Brook Zered and the End of the Wilderness Generation

easy.question: What did Moses command the Israelites to do at the brook Zered?
answers: Rise up and cross it
Camp beside it
Return from it to Kadesh
easy.explanation: Verse 13 says, “Now rise up, and get you over the brook Zered.”

easy.question: How many years passed between leaving Kadesh-barnea and crossing the brook Zered?
answers: Forty years
Thirty-eight years
Seven years
easy.explanation: The passage explicitly says that the period lasted thirty-eight years.

easy.question: Who died before the people continued on their journey?
answers: All the priests
All the people
All the men of war from that generation
easy.explanation: Verse 16 says that all the men of war were consumed and died from among the people.

medium.question: What do the thirty-eight years mentioned in verse 14 explain?
answers: They lasted until the generation of the men of war had come to an end
They were the time spent building the tabernacle
They were the time of the war with Amalek
medium.explanation: The verse connects the thirty-eight years with the end of the generation of fighting men.

medium.question: What does the phrase “to destroy them” mean in the context of “the hand of the Lord was against them”?
answers: To guide them
To strike them or bring them to an end
To lead them
medium.explanation: The context describes the Lord’s hand acting against them until they were consumed, so the phrase means to strike them or bring them to an end.

medium.question: What happened after all the men of war had died?
answers: The people returned to Kadesh-barnea
A new camp was built in the wilderness
The people could continue on their journey
medium.explanation: The verses describe the end of the generation of fighting men, after which the people continued their journey.

challenge.question: What is the main significance of mentioning the thirty-eight years alongside the death of the men of war?
answers: The delay lasted until the judgment against that generation was fulfilled
The people lost their way for many years
The battle at the brook Zered lasted thirty-eight years
challenge.explanation: The verses present this period as the time in which the generation of fighting men came to an end, in accordance with the Lord’s oath.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “until they were consumed” emphasize?
answers: That the punishment was short and temporary
That the process continued until the entire relevant generation had come to an end
That the people defeated all their enemies
challenge.explanation: The wording emphasizes that the process continued until the members of that generation had completely died out.

challenge.question: Which wording shows that the crossing of the brook Zered actually took place rather than remaining only a command?
answers: “As the Lord sware”
“Until all the generation had come to an end”
The change from the command “get you over” to the report “we went over”
challenge.explanation: The passage first gives the command to cross and then reports that the people actually crossed the brook.

questions.question: What is the main significance of mentioning the thirty-eight years alongside the death of the men of war?
answers: The delay lasted until the judgment against that generation was fulfilled
The people lost their way for many years
The battle at the brook Zered lasted thirty-eight years
questions.explanation: The verses present this period as the time in which the generation of fighting men came to an end, in accordance with the Lord’s oath.

questions.question: What does the phrase “until they were consumed” emphasize?
answers: That the punishment was short and temporary
That the process continued until the entire relevant generation had come to an end
That the people defeated all their enemies
questions.explanation: The wording emphasizes that the process continued until the members of that generation had completely died out.

questions.question: Which wording shows that the crossing of the brook Zered actually took place rather than remaining only a command?
answers: “As the Lord sware”
“Until all the generation had come to an end”
The change from the command “get you over” to the report “we went over”
questions.explanation: The passage first gives the command to cross and then reports that the people actually crossed the brook.

paragraphs.title: The Borders of Moab and Ammon and the Inheritance of Peoples

easy.question: What did the Lord command Israel to do when they approached the descendants of Ammon?
answers: Conquer them
Do not besiege or meddle with them
Demand tribute from them
easy.explanation: The Lord commanded, “Distress them not, nor meddle with them.”

easy.question: To whom did the Lord give the land of the descendants of Ammon as an inheritance?
answers: The descendants of Esau
Israel
The descendants of Lot
easy.explanation: The verse says that the land was given to the descendants of Lot.

easy.question: Who lived in the land before the Ammonites?
answers: The Rephaim
The Horims
The Avims
easy.explanation: The passage says that the Rephaim lived there before the Ammonites.

medium.question: What sequence concerning the peoples who lived in these lands is described?
answers: The Ammonites destroyed the descendants of Esau
Israel dispossessed the Horims
Earlier peoples were destroyed, and other peoples inherited their lands and lived in their place
medium.explanation: The verses describe the Rephaim, Horims, and Avims being destroyed, while the Ammonites, descendants of Esau, and Caphtorims settled in their place.

medium.question: What does “Distress them not” mean in “Distress them not, nor meddle with them”?
answers: Do not bless them
Do not besiege them
Do not pass through their land
medium.explanation: The phrase means not to lay siege to them or attack their cities; the following words reinforce that warfare was forbidden.

medium.question: Why does the passage mention that the descendants of Esau and the Caphtorims also inherited lands from other peoples?
answers: To show that the Lord governs the inheritance of lands among other nations as well
To command Israel to fight every nation
To say that all peoples were Israelites
medium.explanation: The comparison with Esau’s descendants and the Caphtorims shows that the Lord also assigned other peoples their places and inheritances.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the Lord’s prohibition against Israel taking the land of Ammon?
answers: Ammon was stronger than Israel
Israel could not cross the border of Moab
Not every land Israel could reach was intended to be its inheritance
challenge.explanation: The Lord had assigned the land of Ammon to the descendants of Lot, so Israel had to respect that boundary and not take it.

challenge.question: What name did the Ammonites give the Rephaim who had lived in their land before them?
answers: Zamzummims
Horims
Caphtorims
challenge.explanation: The passage says that the Ammonites called the Rephaim Zamzummims.

challenge.question: What happened to the Avims and the Caphtorims according to verse 23?
answers: The Avims dispossessed the Caphtorims
The Caphtorims came from Caphtor, destroyed the Avims, and lived in their place
The Israelites destroyed the Avims and settled in Gaza
challenge.explanation: The verse says that the Avims lived as far as Azzah, and that the Caphtorims came from Caphtor, destroyed them, and settled in their place.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the Lord’s prohibition against Israel taking the land of Ammon?
answers: Ammon was stronger than Israel
Israel could not cross the border of Moab
Not every land Israel could reach was intended to be its inheritance
questions.explanation: The Lord had assigned the land of Ammon to the descendants of Lot, so Israel had to respect that boundary and not take it.

questions.question: What name did the Ammonites give the Rephaim who had lived in their land before them?
answers: Zamzummims
Horims
Caphtorims
questions.explanation: The passage says that the Ammonites called the Rephaim Zamzummims.

questions.question: What happened to the Avims and the Caphtorims according to verse 23?
answers: The Avims dispossessed the Caphtorims
The Caphtorims came from Caphtor, destroyed the Avims, and lived in their place
The Israelites destroyed the Avims and settled in Gaza
questions.explanation: The verse says that the Avims lived as far as Azzah, and that the Caphtorims came from Caphtor, destroyed them, and settled in their place.

easy.question: Which river were the Israelites commanded to cross?
answers: The river Arnon
The Jordan River
The river of Egypt
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Pass over the river Arnon.”

easy.question: Who was the king of Heshbon?
answers: Og king of Bashan
Sihon king of the Amorites
Pharaoh king of Egypt
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly names Sihon, king of Heshbon and the Amorites.

easy.question: How would the nations respond when they heard of Israel?
answers: They would help Israel
They would ignore Israel
They would tremble and be in anguish because of Israel
easy.explanation: The verse says that the nations would tremble and be in anguish when they heard of Israel.

medium.question: What sequence of events did the Lord command?
answers: Cross the river Arnon, begin to possess the land, and fight Sihon
Fight Sihon and then return to Egypt
Wait for the nations to fight Israel
medium.explanation: Israel was first told to cross the Arnon, then to begin possessing the land and fight Sihon.

medium.question: What connection does the passage make between the nations hearing of Israel and their response?
answers: The report makes them immediately seek peace
The report makes them afraid and tremble
The report makes them come to Israel’s aid
medium.explanation: The verse says that when the nations hear of Israel, they will tremble and be in anguish.

medium.question: What does “begin to possess it” mean in this context?
answers: Begin to build his land
Begin to flee from his land
Begin to inherit and conquer his land
medium.explanation: The words occur with the command to fight Sihon, so they mean to begin taking possession of the land.

challenge.question: What was added to the promise of victory over Sihon according to verse 25?
answers: The nations would fear and dread Israel
Israel would not need to cross the Arnon
The nations would welcome Israel gladly
challenge.explanation: The verse promises not only victory over Sihon but also that many nations would fear Israel.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “I have given into thine hand” before the battle began?
answers: The battle had already physically ended
The Lord guaranteed Israel’s victory
Israel should give up the battle
challenge.explanation: Although the battle was still ahead, the Lord spoke of Sihon as already delivered into Israel’s hand, guaranteeing victory.

challenge.question: What does “under the whole heaven” emphasize about the nations?
answers: Only nations near the land would hear of Israel
Only the region’s kings would fear Israel
The report and fear would spread among many distant peoples
challenge.explanation: The phrase broadens the scope to many peoples throughout the known world, not merely nearby neighbors.

questions.question: What was added to the promise of victory over Sihon according to verse 25?
answers: The nations would fear and dread Israel
Israel would not need to cross the Arnon
The nations would welcome Israel gladly
questions.explanation: The verse promises not only victory over Sihon but also that many nations would fear Israel.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “I have given into thine hand” before the battle began?
answers: The battle had already physically ended
The Lord guaranteed Israel’s victory
Israel should give up the battle
questions.explanation: Although the battle was still ahead, the Lord spoke of Sihon as already delivered into Israel’s hand, guaranteeing victory.

questions.question: What does “under the whole heaven” emphasize about the nations?
answers: Only nations near the land would hear of Israel
Only the region’s kings would fear Israel
The report and fear would spread among many distant peoples
questions.explanation: The phrase broadens the scope to many peoples throughout the known world, not merely nearby neighbors.

easy.question: To whom did Moses send messengers?
answers: Sihon king of Heshbon
The king of Edom
The king of Moab
easy.explanation: Verse 26 says that Moses sent messengers to Sihon king of Heshbon.

easy.question: What did Moses ask Sihon to allow Israel to do in his land?
answers: Give Israel the whole land
Allow Israel to pass through
Fight Israel immediately
easy.explanation: Moses asked to pass through the land by the highway without turning aside.

easy.question: What did the Israelites promise to pay for food and water?
answers: Gold
Animals
Money
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Thou shalt sell me meat for money” and “give me water for money.”

medium.question: Why did Moses emphasize that he would not turn right or left?
answers: To show that Israel wanted only to pass along the road
To announce that Israel would conquer the whole land
To ask Sihon to guide them
medium.explanation: This emphasis shows that Israel requested a limited and peaceful passage without entering the surrounding territory.

medium.question: What does “Thou shalt sell me meat for money” mean in this context?
answers: You shall break me
You shall sell or provide it to me
You shall drive me away
medium.explanation: In the context of food being purchased, the phrase means to sell or provide food in exchange for money.

medium.question: How did Moses try to show Sihon that his request was reasonable?
answers: He promised to give Sihon the land of Israel
He pointed out that the descendants of Esau and the Moabites had allowed such passage
He said that Sihon was required to obey him
medium.explanation: Moses mentioned that the descendants of Esau and the Moabites had allowed him to pass, presenting his request as peaceful and customary.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the request to buy food and water with money?
answers: The Israelites wanted to make their living only through trade
They did not want to use force to obtain what they needed for the journey
They had no food or water at all
challenge.explanation: Offering payment shows an attempt to travel peacefully and avoid taking supplies by force.

challenge.question: What was the final destination of the journey described in verse 29?
answers: The land beyond the Jordan that the Lord would give Israel
The land of Seir belonging to Esau
Sihon’s city of Heshbon
challenge.explanation: Moses said that they would pass through Sihon’s land until they crossed the Jordan into the land the Lord would give them.

challenge.question: Which detail especially supports the idea that Israel requested temporary passage rather than settlement in Sihon’s land?
answers: They sent messengers
They asked to travel along the road without turning aside
They mentioned the wilderness of Kedemoth
challenge.explanation: The phrases “I will go along by the high way” and “only I will pass through on my feet” emphasize passage rather than settlement.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the request to buy food and water with money?
answers: The Israelites wanted to make their living only through trade
They did not want to use force to obtain what they needed for the journey
They had no food or water at all
questions.explanation: Offering payment shows an attempt to travel peacefully and avoid taking supplies by force.

questions.question: What was the final destination of the journey described in verse 29?
answers: The land beyond the Jordan that the Lord would give Israel
The land of Seir belonging to Esau
Sihon’s city of Heshbon
questions.explanation: Moses said that they would pass through Sihon’s land until they crossed the Jordan into the land the Lord would give them.

questions.question: Which detail especially supports the idea that Israel requested temporary passage rather than settlement in Sihon’s land?
answers: They sent messengers
They asked to travel along the road without turning aside
They mentioned the wilderness of Kedemoth
questions.explanation: The phrases “I will go along by the high way” and “only I will pass through on my feet” emphasize passage rather than settlement.

paragraphs.title: Sihon’s Refusal and the Hardening of His Heart

easy.question: Who was Sihon?
answers: The king of Heshbon
A prophet in Israel
A priest in the sanctuary
easy.explanation: The verse calls Sihon the king of Heshbon.

easy.question: What did Sihon refuse to do?
answers: Fight Israel
Allow Israel to pass through his land
Send messengers to Moses
easy.explanation: The verse says that Sihon would not let Israel pass through his land.

easy.question: Who hardened Sihon’s spirit?
answers: Moses
The Israelites
The Lord God of Israel
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the Lord hardened Sihon’s spirit.

medium.question: What resulted from the hardening of Sihon’s spirit and the making of his heart obstinate?
answers: Sihon agreed to peace
Sihon refused, and eventually was delivered into Israel’s hand
Israel returned to Egypt
medium.explanation: Sihon refused to let Israel pass, and the verse explains that this was so he could be delivered into Israel’s hand.

medium.question: What does “would not” mean in “Sihon king of Heshbon would not let us pass”?
answers: Forgot
Fled
Refused or was unwilling
medium.explanation: In this context, the phrase means that Sihon refused or was unwilling to allow Israel to pass.

medium.question: What was the relationship between Sihon’s refusal and the Lord’s purpose?
answers: His refusal was part of the way he would be delivered into Israel’s hand
His refusal prevented Israel from entering the land
His refusal caused the Lord to punish Moses
medium.explanation: The verse says that the Lord hardened his spirit and made his heart obstinate in order to deliver him into Israel’s hand.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the mention of both Sihon’s “spirit” and his “heart”?
answers: The Lord changed only Sihon’s place of residence
The Lord influenced his inner inclination and his decision
Sihon lost the ability to speak
challenge.explanation: “Spirit” and “heart” describe Sihon’s inner self, emphasizing that his will and decision to refuse were hardened.

challenge.question: What does the phrase “in order that” emphasize in this verse?
answers: The purpose of the Lord’s action
The time when Sihon went to war
The place where Moses lived
challenge.explanation: The phrase introduces a purpose: Sihon’s spirit was hardened so that he would be delivered into Israel’s hand.

challenge.question: What does “as appeareth this day” emphasize?
answers: That the event would happen only in the future
That the event happened before the Exodus
That Sihon’s delivery into Israel’s hand was a present reality at the time of speaking
challenge.explanation: The phrase indicates that the event had already happened or was evident at the time the words were spoken, not merely promised for the future.

questions.question: What can be understood from the mention of both Sihon’s “spirit” and his “heart”?
answers: The Lord changed only Sihon’s place of residence
The Lord influenced his inner inclination and his decision
Sihon lost the ability to speak
questions.explanation: “Spirit” and “heart” describe Sihon’s inner self, emphasizing that his will and decision to refuse were hardened.

questions.question: What does the phrase “in order that” emphasize in this verse?
answers: The purpose of the Lord’s action
The time when Sihon went to war
The place where Moses lived
questions.explanation: The phrase introduces a purpose: Sihon’s spirit was hardened so that he would be delivered into Israel’s hand.

questions.question: What does “as appeareth this day” emphasize?
answers: That the event would happen only in the future
That the event happened before the Exodus
That Sihon’s delivery into Israel’s hand was a present reality at the time of speaking
questions.explanation: The phrase indicates that the event had already happened or was evident at the time the words were spoken, not merely promised for the future.

paragraphs.title: The Lord Commands Israel to Begin Conquering Sihon’s Land

easy.question: To whom did the Lord speak in this verse?
answers: Moses
Sihon
Joshua
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The Lord said unto me,” meaning that He spoke to Moses.

easy.question: Whom did the Lord begin to give before Moses?
answers: Og and his land
Sihon and his land
The children of Israel
easy.explanation: The Lord said that He had begun to give Sihon and his land before Moses.

easy.question: What did the Lord command Israel to do concerning Sihon’s land?
answers: Leave it
Build a city in it
Begin to possess it
easy.explanation: The Lord commanded Israel to begin possessing and inheriting Sihon’s land.

medium.question: What is the relationship between the Lord’s giving Sihon and his land and the command to possess the land?
answers: The giving meant that no action was necessary
The giving was the beginning that enabled Israel to start possessing it
The giving was intended only to warn Sihon
medium.explanation: The Lord announced that He had begun giving Sihon and his land, and immediately commanded Israel to begin possessing it.

medium.question: What does “begin” mean in “begin to possess”?
answers: Start
Hide
Wait
medium.explanation: The word means “start,” and the rest of the command shows that Israel was to begin conquering and inheriting the land.

medium.question: What order of events appears in the verse?
answers: Israel possessed the land, and then the Lord gave it
Sihon gave his land, and then Moses spoke to the Lord
The Lord began giving Sihon and his land, and then commanded Israel to begin possessing it
medium.explanation: First the Lord says that He had begun giving Sihon and his land; afterward He commands Israel to begin possessing it.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “I have begun to give” about the process of inheriting the land?
answers: The process had begun, but Israel still had to act
The process was completely finished
The process had not begun at all
challenge.explanation: The wording shows that the Lord had already begun the process, while the command to begin possessing shows that Israel still had a role to play.

challenge.question: Why are both Sihon and his land mentioned?
answers: To distinguish between two peoples
To show that the promise included both the ruler and the territory he controlled
To say that Sihon would help Israel
challenge.explanation: Mentioning Sihon and his land indicates both the defeat of the ruler and the inheritance of his territory.

challenge.question: What does the use of “possess” teach about how the land would be received?
answers: The land would be received as a gift without any action
The land would remain in Sihon’s hands
The Lord would give the land, but Israel had to act in order to possess it
challenge.explanation: The verse combines the Lord’s gift with Israel’s command to possess the land, showing both divine promise and human action.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “I have begun to give” about the process of inheriting the land?
answers: The process had begun, but Israel still had to act
The process was completely finished
The process had not begun at all
questions.explanation: The wording shows that the Lord had already begun the process, while the command to begin possessing shows that Israel still had a role to play.

questions.question: Why are both Sihon and his land mentioned?
answers: To distinguish between two peoples
To show that the promise included both the ruler and the territory he controlled
To say that Sihon would help Israel
questions.explanation: Mentioning Sihon and his land indicates both the defeat of the ruler and the inheritance of his territory.

questions.question: What does the use of “possess” teach about how the land would be received?
answers: The land would be received as a gift without any action
The land would remain in Sihon’s hands
The Lord would give the land, but Israel had to act in order to possess it
questions.explanation: The verse combines the Lord’s gift with Israel’s command to possess the land, showing both divine promise and human action.

paragraphs.title: Sihon Goes to War and Israel Wins

easy.question: Who came out to fight the Israelites?
answers: Sihon and all his people
Moses alone
The king of Egypt
easy.explanation: The passage says that Sihon came out against Israel with all his people.

easy.question: Where did the battle take place?
answers: Jerusalem
Jahaz
Egypt
easy.explanation: The battle between Israel and Sihon took place at Jahaz.

easy.question: Whom did the Israelites strike?
answers: Only Sihon
Sihon and only his army
Sihon, his sons, and all his people
easy.explanation: The passage specifies that Israel struck Sihon, his sons, and all his people.

medium.question: What happened after Sihon came out to fight Israel?
answers: The Israelites struck him and his people
The Israelites retreated
Sihon conquered Israel
medium.explanation: After Sihon came to fight, the Lord delivered him before Israel, and Israel struck him and his people.

medium.question: What does “came out against us” mean in this passage?
answers: Came behind us
Came toward us
Came into our house
medium.explanation: The phrase means that Sihon came toward Israel or faced them in battle.

medium.question: What was the relationship between the Lord delivering Sihon before Israel and Israel’s victory?
answers: The Lord helped Israel win
Sihon fled before the battle
Israel did not fight at all
medium.explanation: The passage attributes the victory to the Lord’s delivering Sihon before Israel, after which Israel struck him and his people.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the fact that Sihon came with “all his people”?
answers: He came alone
The conflict involved entire groups, not just their leaders
He was unprepared for war
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that the battle involved Sihon and his people, not merely a personal confrontation between leaders.

challenge.question: What sequence of events is described in these verses?
answers: Sihon came to fight, the Lord delivered him before Israel, and Israel struck him
Israel struck Sihon, and afterward he went to war
The Lord delivered Israel to Sihon, and Sihon struck them
challenge.explanation: That is the exact sequence: Sihon came to fight, the Lord delivered him before Israel, and Israel struck him and his people.

challenge.question: Which detail emphasizes that the victory was complete?
answers: The battle took place at Jahaz
Sihon came toward Israel
Sihon, his sons, and all his people were struck
challenge.explanation: Mentioning Sihon, his sons, and all his people shows that not only the king but also his family and nation were defeated.

paragraphs.title: Capturing and Devoting the Cities to Destruction

easy.question: What did the Israelites do to all the enemy cities at that time?
answers: They captured them all
They abandoned them all
They built new cities
easy.explanation: The verse says, “We took all his cities at that time.”

easy.question: Whom did the Israelites not leave alive in the captured cities?
answers: Only the kings
The men, women, and little ones
Only the soldiers
easy.explanation: The passage explicitly mentions the men, women, and little ones.

easy.question: What did the Israelites do with the cattle?
answers: Left them in the cities
Returned them to the enemy
Took them as spoil for themselves
easy.explanation: The passage says, “Only the cattle we took for a prey unto ourselves.”

medium.question: What sequence of events does the passage describe?
answers: First they captured the cities, and then they destroyed their inhabitants
First they took the cattle, and then they built cities
First they spared the people, and then they fled
medium.explanation: The passage first says that they captured all the cities and then describes the destruction of their inhabitants.

medium.question: What does “none to remain” mean in this passage?
answers: A treasure
A survivor or remnant
A large city
medium.explanation: In this context, the phrase means that no person or remnant was left alive.

medium.question: What does “Only” at the beginning of verse 35 teach?
answers: No cities were captured
The women and children were spared
The cattle and property were exceptions
medium.explanation: “Only” introduces an exception: after the people were destroyed, Israel was allowed to take the cattle and the spoil of the cities.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “the men, and the women, and the little ones, of every city”?
answers: The destruction included all kinds of inhabitants, regardless of age or sex
Only residents of the largest cities were affected
Only the soldiers were taken captive
challenge.explanation: The passage lists men, women, and little ones to emphasize that the entire population was included.

challenge.question: What was the main difference between the fate of the people and the fate of the property?
answers: Both the people and the property were left where they were
The people were devoted to destruction, while the cattle and spoil were taken
The people were taken as spoil, while the property was destroyed
challenge.explanation: No people were left alive, while the Israelites took the cattle and the spoil of the cities for themselves.

challenge.question: Why does “Only” limit the destruction described in the previous verse?
answers: Because it adds another group that was destroyed
Because it changes the meaning of “cities”
Because it identifies an exception: not everything was destroyed, since the cattle and property were taken
challenge.explanation: “Only” contrasts the destruction of the people with the preservation of certain property for Israel’s use.

answers: The destruction included all kinds of inhabitants, regardless of age or sex

paragraphs.title: The Extent of the Conquest and the Boundary Not Crossed

easy.question: Who gave Israel all the land before them?
answers: The Lord their God
The descendants of Ammon
The king of Gilead
easy.explanation: The verse says, “The Lord our God delivered all unto us.”

easy.question: Where did the conquered area begin according to verse 36?
answers: At Gilead
At Aroer beside the river Arnon
In the land of the descendants of Ammon
easy.explanation: The verse describes the area as beginning at Aroer, by the brink of the river Arnon.

easy.question: Which land did the Israelites not approach?
answers: The land of Gilead
The land by the river Arnon
The land of the descendants of Ammon
easy.explanation: Verse 37 explicitly says that Israel did not approach the land of the descendants of Ammon.

medium.question: What area is described as having no city too strong for Israel?
answers: From Aroer to Gilead
From the river Jabbok to the land of Ammon
Only within the land of Ammon
medium.explanation: Verse 36 describes the area from Aroer by the Arnon to Gilead.

medium.question: Why did Israel not approach the land of Ammon?
answers: They had no weapons
Because the Lord their God had commanded them not to
Because the land was too far away
medium.explanation: The verse says that Israel avoided the land of Ammon because the Lord had forbidden it.

medium.question: What does “too strong for us” mean in this passage?
answers: It disappeared from us
It was near us
It was stronger or more fortified than we were
medium.explanation: The phrase means that a city was strong or fortified; the context says that no such city could withstand Israel.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the mention of the rivers Arnon and Jabbok?
answers: The rivers served as geographic boundary markers for the conquered areas
Israel crossed every river in the land
The rivers were large cities
challenge.explanation: The rivers are mentioned alongside regions and cities, so they function as landmarks for boundaries and territories.

challenge.question: What is the main idea of verses 36–37 taken together?
answers: Israel conquered only one city
Israel won a large territory but stopped where the Lord commanded
Israel conquered no territory east of the Jordan
challenge.explanation: The passage says that the whole area as far as Gilead was given to Israel, while also emphasizing that they did not approach Ammon as commanded.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that the victory did not result solely from Israel’s military strength?
answers: The mention of the mountain cities
The mention of the river Arnon
The statement that the Lord delivered everything before them
challenge.explanation: The verse attributes Israel’s success to the Lord, saying that He delivered everything before them.
